timeline.current_model: ERK2/MAPK1 is a dual-specificity-regulated serine/threonine kinase that is activated by MEK1/2-mediated dual phosphorylation on TEY residues, triggering global conformational changes that enhance catalytic activity; phospho-ERK2 homodimerizes and translocates to the nucleus by binding directly to nuclear pore complex nucleoporins (carrier-independent), while in resting cells it is held in the cytoplasm via a C-terminal retention sequence that mediates MEK1 association; in the nucleus it phosphorylates substrates (e.g., ELK-1, PARP1-associated IEG promoters, Par3, CPEB4) docked through a conserved acidic-patch/hydrophobic-groove KIM-docking site, and in the cytoplasm it phosphorylates diverse substrates including PFAS (stimulating de novo purine synthesis), ULK1 (triggering its ubiquitin-dependent degradation and limiting mitophagy), PAK1 (negative feedback), Shank3 (promoting degradation), and Par3 (regulating axon polarity); its activity is spatially organized by scaffold proteins such as IQGAP1, nesprin-2 (at PML nuclear bodies), and MEKK1, and is negatively regulated by phosphatases (MKP3/DUSP6) that engage the same KIM docking groove, with conformational selection by small-molecule inhibitors further modulating dephosphorylation susceptibility.

molecular_activity.term_label: catalytic activity, acting on a protein
